overview: SwitchAura is the multi-target mode of Nekoware's Aura module, with a randomized click-speed draw, a C07 release before each hit and a block re-arm that is a local flag only: no C08 arm packet is ever sent, so the server-side blocking state never exists and the releases are unsolicited. The wire carries periodic C02 attacks and C0A swings plus the stray C07s, and the pre-motion rotation keeps the C03 look aligned with each target.

sections.p: The click speed is drawn per attack cycle: when the Click Speed setting (default 12, range 1-20) exceeds 2, the effective rate is MathUtils.getRandom(cps - 2, cps), a uniform draw in [cps-2, cps) via a fresh Random, so at the default the period jitters between roughly 10 and 12 attacks per second. The static Timer is a real period with reset(), anchored at class load like SingleAura's, so the first attack fires on the first expired pre-motion event after enable. On each expiry the pre-motion branch sends C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM (BlockPos.ORIGIN, face DOWN) when autoBlock and Aura.isBlocking hold, then swings and queues a C02 ATTACK through sendQueue.addToSendQueue, which flushes at the end of the tick.

The post-motion branch re-arms blocking by setting the shared static Aura.isBlocking to true when canBlockSword passes, but nothing sends a C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement: the server never transitions to the using-item state, so the C07 releases in the next cycle are releases without a preceding use, which vanilla processPlayerDigging just consumes as a no-op item-use clear. When the target disappears, stopServerBlocking emits one final C07 release. The Auto Block setting is therefore cosmetic: no server-side blocking, no damage reduction, and the releases are the only autoblock artifact on the wire.

Like SingleAura, the aim comes from RotationUtils.getRotations (target eye height halved) and is written into the pre-motion update yaw and pitch, carried by that tick's C03, plus rotationYawHead, rotationPitchHead and renderYawOffset. Because the mode re-targets every cycle and getTarget returns the first in-range entity in list order, the rotation snaps between whatever entity happens to lead the list when the timer expires, giving the switch pattern its name.

files.label: SwitchAura.java
files.explanation: The mode: the randomized click-speed draw, the pre-motion C07 release plus C02 attack, the post-motion local-only block re-arm that never sends C08, and the target-loss release cleanup.

files.label: Aura.java (parent dispatcher)
files.explanation: The parent module that routes modes and owns the shared state: isMode routing to SingleAura, SwitchAura and MultiAura, the settings (Click Speed, Range, Rots, Auto Block, target filters) the mode reads through getBool and getDouble, and onDisable, which reads SingleAura.unblock to emit its release packet.

countering.label: Reach (post-look ray trace)
countering.explanation: Grim's Reach queues each C02 attack with the player's position and scores it on the next look update: the eye position is ray-traced against the compensated entity box (threshold 0.0005, plus 0.1 hitbox margin for 1.8 clients and the movement threshold), and any intercept distance above the server attribute reach (3.0) flags, with a cancelBuffer that aggressively cancels the next four hits after one flag. The module's Range setting spans 3.0-6.0, so hits from the outer band flag at the attack tick while close-in hits pass. The pre-motion rotation does not help: the check measures distance, not angle.

countering.label: FightHitbox (deferred combat ray)
countering.explanation: FightHitbox stores each InteractEntityEvent and performs the ray trace on the next MoveEvent because 1.8 sends the attack before the yaw update; for 1.8 clients it uses the HawkPlayer's own yaw with the victim at the lag-compensated history location, and maxReach defaults to 3.1 with the eye at +1.62. The module's pre-motion rotation puts the C03 look exactly on the target, so the ray hits the box, and any hit whose eye-to-box distance exceeds 3.1 flags. At the default Range 4 this is a real counter: center-to-center distance 4 with a 0.6-wide victim leaves roughly 3.4 to the box edge, over the 3.1 bound, so the switch mode cannot attack at its configured reach without tripping it.

countering.label: Fight Direction (attack-ray alignment)
countering.explanation: Direction runs a combinedDirectionCheck ray from the player's eye position against the damaged entity's box with the configured loop and angle precision, and it is the alignment check for the attack stream: the C03-carried look must point at the victim. Because the module writes its aim pre-motion, each C02 lands with a matching look and the ray hits, so the check rewards while Rots is on; with Rots off, the divergence between real look and attack target accumulates violation. The entry is the honest boundary: the module's own rotation is what keeps this check and Hawk's direction checks quiet.

countering.label: KillAura Speed ledger (C02 rate)
countering.explanation: The Speed ledger is where this mode differs from SingleAura: checkFrequency counts C02 ATTACK packets against max-attack-packets (20/s) at receipt, and the damage-event path counts every C02 USE_ENTITY into totalAttacks against max-attacks (16/s). At Click Speed 20 the randomized draw of 18-20 attacks per second pushes totalAttacks over 16 each second once damage events land, so the maxed setting trips the Speed branch; at the default 12 the 10-12/s draw passes both ledgers. The NoSwing branch (max-swing-time 80ms) stays silent because every C02 is preceded by swingItem, and the Direction and Reach branches behave as in the single-target analysis.
